MoE roofline, corrected TWICE. (a) Original in-conversation estimate used 2B/param and omitted the gate matrix (~2.7x too high). (b) The first 'correction' then wrongly divided the NO-MTP forward rate by the MTP accept multiplier. Final numbers: per expert gate+up+down = 4,915,200 params (hidden 2560, moe_inter 640); active = 10 experts x 48 layers = 2.36B params/token (+0.24B shared) = 2.6B -> at NVFP4 0.5B/param = 1.30 GB/token -> /273 GB/s = 4.75 ms/token -> ~210 tok/s ceiling. MEASURED: no-MTP 56.6 tok/s = 56.6 forwards/s = 17.67 ms/forward = 73.6 GB/s = ~27% of peak (NOT 11% - that error divided by the accept multiplier). MTP3: 91 tok/s at accept 2.46 (LDB-measured, '37.0 steps x 2.43') = 37.0 fwd/s = 27.0 ms/forward. MTP VERIFICATION CAVEAT: a multi-token forward evaluates ~4 token positions, each selecting its own top-10 experts (up to ~40 distinct, less overlap), so its weight traffic is between 1.30 GB (perfect overlap) and ~5.19 GB (none) => 18-70% of peak. MTP may be CLOSER to the bandwidth wall than no-MTP. CONFIRMED CONCLUSION: decode is not at a hard roofline (2.3-3.7x headroom on the no-MTP path), so the limiter is kernel/dispatch efficiency, not raw DRAM bandwidth.
